ai.literal: Excellence it yields and wealth it yields; than virtue greater gain what is there to a soul?
ai.translation: Virtue yields both glory and wealth. What greater gain can there be for a living being?
ai.modern: ஒருவருக்குச் சிறப்பையும் செல்வத்தையும் தரக்கூடிய அறத்தை விட, உயிர்களுக்கு மேலான நன்மை வேறு என்ன இருக்கிறது?
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the supreme value of virtue (அறம்). It states that virtue is the source of both worldly prosperity (செல்வம்) and ultimate glory or excellence (சிறப்பு). Because it provides these two fundamental benefits, the poet asks rhetorically what greater gain (ஆக்கம்) could possibly exist for any living soul. The word 'ஊங்கு' means 'greater than' or 'beyond', reinforcing that nothing surpasses virtue in bringing good to life.

ai.literal: Than virtue greater wealth is not; it than forgetting greater is not ruin.
ai.translation: There is no greater wealth than virtue, and no greater ruin than forgetting it.
ai.modern: அறத்தை விடச் சிறந்த செல்வமும் இல்லை, அந்த அறத்தை மறப்பதை விடப் பெரிய அழிவும் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet establishes virtue as the ultimate source of prosperity and its neglect as the ultimate cause of destruction. The word ஆக்கம் means wealth, growth, or prosperity, showing that virtue brings tangible good to one's life. Conversely, கேடு means ruin or destruction, warning that merely forgetting to practice virtue leads directly to one's downfall.

ai.literal: possible by the manner virtuous deed without ceasing going place all should do
ai.translation: Perform virtuous deeds without ceasing, in every possible way and at every available opportunity.
ai.modern: உங்களால் முடிந்த வழிகளில் எல்லாம், வாய்ப்பு கிடைக்கும் இடங்களில் எல்லாம், இடைவிடாமல் அறச்செயல்களைச் செய்ய வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet urges continuous and practical commitment to virtue. The word 'ஒல்லும்' means what is possible, suggesting that one should do good deeds according to their own capacity and means. 'செல்லும் வாய்' refers to every place or opportunity one encounters in life. Together, the couplet teaches that practicing virtue is not limited to specific times or grand gestures, but should be a constant, unceasing effort in everyday situations.

ai.literal: In the mind blemish without-he being, all that virtue; empty-show nature-of others.
ai.translation: Being spotless in one's mind is the entirety of virtue. All else is merely the nature of empty show.
ai.modern: ஒருவன் தன் மனத்தில் குற்றம் இல்லாதவனாக இருப்பதே முழுமையான அறமாகும். மற்றவை எல்லாம் வெறும் ஆரவாரத் தன்மை கொண்டவை.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the core of virtue as inner purity. The phrase 'மனத்துக்கண் மாசிலன் ஆதல்' emphasizes that true righteousness is simply the state of being free from mental blemishes. The word 'அனைத்து' asserts that this inner purity constitutes the entirety of virtue. Everything else ('பிற'), such as outward displays of goodness, is dismissed as 'ஆகுல நீர', meaning they are of the nature of noisy, empty show.

ai.literal: Envy, desire, anger, harsh word, all four, without slipping into, that which proceeds is virtue.
ai.translation: Virtue is that which is practiced without slipping into these four: envy, desire, anger, and harsh words.
ai.modern: பொறாமை, ஆசை, சினம், கடுஞ்சொல் ஆகிய இந்த நான்கிலும் வழுவி விழாமல் நடப்பதே அறமாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the core of virtuous conduct by identifying four destructive traits to avoid. Envy, excessive desire, anger, and harsh words are presented as flaws that corrupt one's character. The word 'இழுக்கா' (without slipping) suggests that these traits are like slippery ground that can easily cause a person to fall from the right path. True virtue is the active effort of conducting one's life without yielding to these four negative forces.

ai.literal: 'Later we will know' without saying, may you do virtue; indeed that [is at] perishing time [an] undying companion.
ai.translation: Do not delay doing good by saying 'We will see to it later.' When the time comes for you to die, virtue will be your only undying companion.
ai.modern: 'பிறகு பார்த்துக்கொள்ளலாம்' என்று காலம் கடத்தாமல் இப்போதே அறத்தைச் செய்யுங்கள். ஒருவருடைய உயிர் பிரியும் காலத்தில் அவருக்கு அழியாத துணையாக இருப்பது அந்த அறம் மட்டுமே.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against the common human tendency to postpone doing good. The phrase 'aṉṟu aṟivām' captures the excuse of putting off virtue until later in life. The poet urges the reader to practice virtue immediately without making such excuses. The striking contrast between 'poṉṟum kāl' (the time of perishing) and 'poṉṟā tuṇai' (an imperishable companion) highlights that when the body dies, only one's accumulated virtue remains as an eternal support.

ai.literal: Of virtue, the path is this, saying is not needed; between the palanquin with the one who bears and the one who rides.
ai.translation: There is no need to explain that this is the path of virtue; just look at the difference between the palanquin bearer and the rider.
ai.modern: அறத்தின் வழி இதுதான் என்று சொல்லத் தேவையில்லை; பல்லக்கைத் தூக்குபவனுக்கும் அதில் ஏறிச் செல்பவனுக்கும் இடையே உள்ள வேறுபாட்டைப் பார்த்தாலே தெரியும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet illustrates the visible consequences of virtue. The poet states that one does not need words to explain the path of virtue. The contrast between the person riding in the palanquin and the person bearing it serves as a living example. The rider enjoys the fruits of virtuous deeds, while the bearer experiences the burden of lacking them.

ai.literal: Missed day without occurring good if [one] does, that [is for] a person living days' path blocking stone.
ai.translation: If one does good without letting a single day go to waste, that virtue will be the stone that blocks their path of future births.
ai.modern: ஒருவன் அறம் செய்யத் தவறிய நாள் ஒன்று கூட ஏற்படாதவாறு தொடர்ந்து நற்செயல்களைச் செய்தால், அந்த அறமே அவனது பிறவி வழியை அடைக்கும் கல்லாக மாறும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the importance of practicing virtue continuously. The phrase 'வீழ்நாள்' refers to a day that falls away or is wasted without doing good. If a person ensures that not a single day passes without performing a virtuous act, that accumulated virtue acts as a powerful barrier. The poet compares this virtue to a stone ('கல்') that firmly blocks the path of living days ('வாழ்நாள் வழி'). While 'வாழ்நாள்' literally means 'days of life', in this context it signifies the endless cycle of rebirths. Thus, relentless virtue is the key to ending worldly suffering.

ai.literal: Through virtue that which comes indeed (is) joy; other all are on the outside, and fame they are without.
ai.translation: Only that which comes through virtue is true joy. All else is extraneous and devoid of fame.
ai.modern: அறவழியில் வருவதே உண்மையான இன்பமாகும். மற்றவை எல்லாம் இன்பத்திற்குப் புறம்பானவை; அவற்றுக்குப் புகழும் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines true happiness by stating that only the joy arising from virtuous conduct is genuine. The emphatic particle 'ஏ' in 'வருவதே' stresses that absolutely nothing else qualifies as true joy. Everything else ('மற்று எல்லாம்') falls outside this definition ('புறத்த') and brings neither real happiness nor lasting fame ('புகழும் இல').

ai.literal: That which is to be done, examining, is virtue alone for one; that which is to be escaped, examining, is blame.
ai.translation: If one examines what a person ought to do, it is virtue alone; if one examines what must be avoided, it is vice.
ai.modern: ஒருவன் தன் வாழ்வில் செய்யத் தகுந்தது அறம் மட்டுமே; அவன் தப்பித்துத் தவிர்க்க வேண்டியது பழி தரும் செயல்களே ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the fundamental choice in human action. The word 'ceyal' refers to doing, while 'uyal' refers to escaping or avoiding; both are joined with 'palatu' to mean 'that which is of the nature of'. The repeated word 'orum' implies that careful examination will always lead to this conclusion. By using the emphatic suffix 'e' in 'arane', the text stresses that virtue is the only true course of action, dividing all deeds simply into virtue to be practiced and blame to be shunned.
